title: Temporal dequant amortization + fused attention microkernel with KV alignment
author: Sofia Marin
description: Motivation: Dequantization work is a material token-level cost in quantized inference (INT8/FP8). Existing dequant+matmul+requant sequences introduce extra memory traffic and duplicate per-token scaling that becomes significant for long contexts and continuous-batching workloads. This PR implements a set of complementary changes: (1) a fused attention microkernel that accepts quantized inputs with packed per-head scaling metadata and emits quantized outputs without a separate dequant/requant roundtrip; (2) a temporal dequant amortization layer that caches and reuses per-head/per-key scale factors across contiguous KV windows; and (3) KV cache alignment logic so cached keys/values and their scale metadata remain coherent across prefix-shared requests and continuous batching. The goal is to reduce token-level dequant overhead while preserving numerical fidelity for INT8/FP8 models.
commits: b28c9d2: expose per_head_scale metadata in runtime request blob and persistence format
d4f7e9a: temporal scale cache implementation and TTL eviction policy
e52b730: KV cache alignment logic and migration handler for previous cache format
f6c3a11: scheduler changes to make continuous-batching aware of temporal amortization
09ad57b: unit tests and integration perf harness updates
ci_checks: bench-suite: initial perf run showed a regression in short-seq throughput; fixed in follow-up commit and clean run shows improvements
review_comments: Arjun: Can you explain how per_head_scale is stored in the request blob? Risk: making blob larger could regress small-payload throughput — author: per_head_scale is optional and only present for quantized models; it's delta-compressed and only attached to first token in a KV window.

Evelyn: Numeric drift on FP8 models was visible in the initial microkernel; author: adjusted accumulation path and added 16-bit accumulation for attention softmax (see fused_attn_int8.cu lines ~220-260), reduced max delta to 1e-3 relative to baseline in our eval set.

Miguel: How do you ensure cache entries don't leak across tenants? author: scale_cache respects tenant IDs and uses the existing KV cache eviction + namespace keys; migration tool converts old caches to namespaced entries during rollout.
Arjun (follow-up): Please add telemetry for amortization hit-rate — author: added metrics runtime.kv.scale_cache.hits and .misses and a continuous-batcher tag for amortized requests.
ci_notes: There was a short red on the bench-suite due to an incorrect vectorized path for 1-token sequences; fixed in commit e52b730. After rerun, the bench-suite shows consistent improvements on INT8 and parity on FP8 numerical fidelity targets.
benchmarks_summary: Microbenchmarks on A100 (p4d-style hardware) with batch sizes 1..64 and sequences up to 8192 tokens: INT8 end-to-end token latency reduced by 9-15% median and p99 improved by up to 18% on long sequences (>=2048). Throughput for sustained streaming workloads increased 12-22% depending on sequence length and batching configuration. FP8 variants show 4-7% improvements (mostly from reduced memory traffic) with <0.2% absolute change on per-token perplexity in our eval set. Amortization hit rate in canary traffic averaged 78% (higher on chat-like workloads).
rollout_plan: Canary on non-production tenant group (10% traffic) for 72h with telemetry checks: kv.scale_cache.hits, p99 latency, and numeric regression alerts. Gradual ramp to 50% over 48h if no alerts; full rollout behind a runtime flag. Migration tool will be run as part of the controller rollout to convert existing KV cache entries; fallbacks available to disable temporal amortization per-tenant.
migration_and_backward_compatibility: Included a migration tool (serving/runtime/integration/kv_migration_tool.py) that can convert existing cached KV blobs to include per_head_scale entries. Runtime supports both old and new cache formats; if new format not present the fused kernel falls back to the legacy dequant path. This ensures safe rollback.
testing_notes: Added unit tests for scale_cache eviction semantics and TTL; added integration tests that replay recorded chat sessions to validate scale reuse; extended bench harness to compare fused kernel vs baseline in identical scheduling conditions.
release_notes: Performance: Reduced dequantization overhead for quantized models via fused attention microkernel and temporal amortization. Observable improvements in INT8 throughput & latency for streaming/continuous-batching workloads. Safe rollout with runtime flag and migration tool.
merge_commit_msg:
squash: temporal dequant amortization + fused attn kernel; add scale cache and KV alignment

Significant performance improvement for quantized inference by eliminating repeated dequant/requant cycles and reusing per-head scales across KV windows. Includes migration tool and telemetry.
